summary: Any array position can contain the sole unpaired value, so exact identification requires reading all n entries in the worst case. One XOR per entry matches that lower bound.

optimality.argument: Suppose an algorithm leaves some position unread. The other n - 1 positions can consist entirely of valid equal pairs, while the unread position can contain either of two different singleton values. Both completed arrays satisfy the frequency promise and agree on every inspected position, yet their answers differ. Therefore every position must be inspected in the worst case, giving Omega(n). The current XOR fold performs constant work per entry, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing an unread singleton position changes the required answer while leaving all inspected paired values unchanged.
The implementation visits every input value once and performs one constant-time XOR update.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover reordered pairs, a negative-free multi-pair input, and the one-element minimum; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
